verdict.reasoning: Patient states, 'I've been having diarrhea for like, let's say, past three days, more or less.'
When asked how many times a day, patient says, 'Yeah, around five to six times a day.' and confirms stools are 'definitely watery. Loose stools.'
Patient reports, 'it started with vomiting, so I vomited a couple of times, but then that went away. And, yeah, it's just diarrhea now.' and confirms vomiting has stopped.
Patient says, 'I feel very dehydrated.' and 'I feel very weak, though.' and also, 'I don't really feel like I have appetite,' which the doctor restates as 'your appetite is reduced.'
In response to 'Any blood in your stools?', patient answers, 'No, not that I could see.'
Regarding fever/temperature, patient says, 'Probably at the beginning I was feeling I had a bit of temperature, but now I feel kind of fine.' This supports that they currently deny fever.
When asked, 'Any headaches or muscle pains?', patient replies, 'Not really.' which includes headache.
The same response 'Not really.' to 'Any headaches or muscle pains?' covers denial of muscle pain.
Patient states, 'I do suffer of asthma.'
Patient says about asthma, 'so I do have my nailers that I, you know, I use infrequently,' and confirms 'Yes, it is.' when asked if it is a blue inhaler.
Patient reports, 'My father ... used to have high blood pressure. He actually died of bowel cancer like 10 years ago.'
Patient says of mother, 'she has diabetes.' and clarifies, 'It's type two.'
Patient states, 'Oh, I live alone.' and later, 'I'm a software engineer.'
On alcohol and smoking, patient says, 'Not really. I drink infrequently, like socially, let's say, and I don't smoke.'
Doctor concludes, 'I think you're probably suffering from what we call gastroenteritis, okay.'

Doctor explains, 'gastroenteritis ... is just a tummy bug. It's an infection of your tummy and normally lasts for about three to five days', consistent with a viral-type infection causing diarrhea, initial vomiting, and dehydration as described by patient.
Doctor advises, 'you can drink plenty of fluids, really try and flush the toxins out your body.'

Doctor says, 'You can get things from the pharmacy, which called Diurelite, which can help replenish any minerals and vitamins you may have lost. It's called Diurelite. It's a type of fluid replacement drink.'
Doctor recommends, 'You can take some paracetamol if you're feeling feverish and weak.'
Doctor states, 'Would probably advise you to continue taking time off work for next day or two until you get better.' and patient agrees to rest.
Doctor instructs, 'Let's see how the next few days go. And if you're still not better next week, I want you to come back and see me and we can have another look at your symptoms.'
